data.title: Wondering Why Zip Co Fell? Here's What The Bears Saw
data.description:
If you had glanced at Zip Co on 1 January 2026 and decided to sit it out while analysts argued over whether it deserved a richer multiple or a sharp discount, the outcome would have looked very different to the upbeat narratives on both sides. For Zip Co shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 49.7%, including dividends. Faced with that split between bullish buyback optimism and regulatory worry, which assumption would you have challenged first?

On Simply Wall St, a Narrative is an investor's thesis written down: the reasoning, plus the numbers it rests on. Run those numbers and you get an estimated Fair Value.

The Two Zip Co Stories Investors Were Pricing In

The shares cost A$3.29 at the start of the period, and Zip Co sat between two very different stories about what might come next.

On the optimistic side, analysts saw a Fair Value of A$4.58, or 39% above the start price. This was built on an assumption of 17.4% annual revenue growth supported by partnerships such as Google Pay and Stripe.

The pessimistic view put Fair Value closer to A$2.1, or 36% below the start price. This view focused on the risk that tighter US and Australian regulation could lift compliance costs and restrict new product launches.

What The Zip Co Numbers Actually Tested

Zip Co reported H2 2026 revenue of A$677.895 million and net income of A$64.031 million, both higher than H2 2025, which gave the optimistic growth story some backing. Net margin slipped from 10.1% to 9.4%, so the cleaner profitability path assumed in the bullish case was not fully in evidence. The period cut both ways.

The episode turned on one simple assumption: that higher volume would quickly translate into fatter margins. When you assess another fintech, track revenue, profit and net margin together to see whether scale is improving economics or just making the top line bigger.

What Zip Co's Drop Now Asks You To Believe

Zip Co changes hands at A$1.69, after a share price that declined 49.7% from the start of the year. The analyst consensus narrative on Simply Wall St still places its fair value above that level and ties the gap to how credibly fraud control and U.S. expansion support future profitability.

For the fall to look like an opening instead of a warning sign, a buyer today would need to believe Zip Co can keep fraud losses contained while using AI-led underwriting and U.S. partnerships to support cash earnings.

"The main factor that has to go right is that Zip Co continues to balance new product rollout and active customer growth with tight credit control, especially in the U.S. Pay in Z portfolio. Current valuation suggests the market is discounting Zip Co's guidance for FY27 cash EBTDA of $340 million and ongoing buybacks, so the share price reflects scepticism that recent earnings and margin changes will continue."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for

After Zip Co, One Step Away

Zip Co lives on digital spending and credit outcomes. Your next question could be where that money sometimes ends up.

Plenty of customers eventually want exposure to real assets. One familiar route is straightforward. They buy gold.

Someone still has to find, develop and operate the deposits meeting that demand. One miner is shifting from exploration toward regular production at a single project.

That move changes the dynamic. The story tilts away from discovery and toward turning a defined resource into repeatable cash flow.

The open question is how smoothly that transition unfolds and who ultimately benefits.

data.title: How Investors May Respond To Clorox (CLX) Thin Dividend Coverage
data.description:

  • The declared payout comes as Clorox's dividend has recently exceeded free cash flow at about 133%, which points to pressure on cash generation while a new CEO prepares to take charge in January 2027.

Scan how Clorox's stretched payout compares with other income ideas by reviewing our hand-picked 8 dividend fortresses built for dividend-focused investors who watch cash coverage closely.

Clorox Investment Narrative Recap

To own Clorox, you effectively need to believe the health and hygiene focus, ERP optimization and GOJO integration described in the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St can support steady earnings while consumers keep trading down and shopping club and mass channels. The biggest near term swing factor remains how quickly productivity and mix help margins cope with over US$200 million of forecast cost inflation.

The key risk right now is cash generation. Dividend payouts are running at about 133% of free cash flow and roughly 85% to 90% of net earnings, which tightens room to invest while servicing debt that is not well covered by operating cash flow. If margin rebuilding stalls, capital allocation options narrow.

The US$1.25 quarterly dividend affirmation is the clearest touchpoint for that cash flow story. It keeps roughly US$600 million of annual dividend commitments in place even as free cash flow coverage remains thin and supply chain and input costs are guided to be significantly above historical levels in fiscal 2027.

For you as an income focused holder, this payout decision keeps the dividend stream intact for now but also concentrates attention on execution under the incoming CEO from January 2027. data.title: We Think Euvic's (WSE:EUV) Robust Earnings Are Conservative
data.description:
Euvic S.A. (WSE:EUV) announced strong profits, but the stock was stagnant. Our analysis suggests that this might be because shareholders have noticed some concerning underlying factors.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

Examining Cashflow Against Euvic's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). In plain english, this ratio subtracts FCF from net profit, and divides that number by the company's average operating assets over that period. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

Therefore, it's actually considered a good thing when a company has a negative accrual ratio, but a bad thing if its accrual ratio is positive. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Over the twelve months to September 2026, Euvic recorded an accrual ratio of -0.65. That indicates that its free cash flow quite significantly exceeded its statutory profit. To wit, it produced free cash flow of zł118m during the period, dwarfing its reported profit of zł23.4m. Notably, Euvic had negative free cash flow last year, so the zł118m it produced this year was a welcome improvement. Notably, the company has issued new shares, thus diluting existing shareholders and reducing their share of future earnings.

Note: we always recommend investors check balance sheet strength. Click here to be taken to our balance sheet analysis of Euvic.

To understand the value of a company's earnings growth, it is imperative to consider any dilution of shareholders' interests. In fact, Euvic increased the number of shares on issue by 1,606% over the last twelve months by issuing new shares. As a result, its net income is now split between a greater number of shares. To talk about net income, without noticing earnings per share, is to be distracted by the big numbers while ignoring the smaller numbers that talk to per share value. You can see a chart of Euvic's EPS by clicking here.

How Is Dilution Impacting Euvic's Earnings Per Share (EPS)?

We don't have any data on the company's profits from three years ago. And so, you can see quite clearly that dilution is having a rather significant impact on shareholders.

If Euvic's EPS can grow over time then that drastically improves the chances of the share price moving in the same direction. However, if its profit increases while its earnings per share stay flat (or even fall) then shareholders might not see much benefit. For that reason, you could say that EPS is more important that net income in the long run, assuming the goal is to assess whether a company's share price might grow.

Our Take On Euvic's Profit Performance

In conclusion, Euvic has a strong cashflow relative to earnings, which indicates good quality earnings, but the dilution means its earnings per share are dropping faster than its profit. Based on these factors, it's hard to tell if Euvic's profits are a reasonable reflection of its underlying profitability. data.title: Shareholders Will Be Pleased With The Quality of Pierce Group's (STO:PIERCE) Earnings
data.description:
Pierce Group AB (publ)'s (STO:PIERCE) earnings announcement last week was disappointing for investors, despite the decent profit numbers. We did some digging and actually think they are being unnecessarily pessimistic.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Zooming In On Pierce Group's Earnings

As finance nerds would already know, the accrual ratio from cashflow is a key measure for assessing how well a company's free cash flow (FCF) matches its profit. To get the accrual ratio we first subtract FCF from profit for a period, and then divide that number by the average operating assets for the period. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. While having an accrual ratio above zero is of little concern, we do think it's worth noting when a company has a relatively high accrual ratio. Notably, there is some academic evidence that suggests that a high accrual ratio is a bad sign for near-term profits, generally speaking.

Pierce Group has an accrual ratio of -0.12 for the year to September 2026. Therefore, its statutory earnings were quite a lot less than its free cashflow. In fact, it had free cash flow of kr102m in the last year, which was a lot more than its statutory profit of kr46.0m. Given that Pierce Group had negative free cash flow in the prior corresponding period, the trailing twelve month resul of kr102m would seem to be a step in the right direction.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Pierce Group's Profit Performance

Pierce Group's accrual ratio is solid, and indicates strong free cash flow, as we discussed, above. Based on this observation, we consider it likely that Pierce Group's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! And it's also positive that the company showed enough improvement to book a profit this year, after losing money last year. The goal of this article has been to assess how well we can rely on the statutory earnings to reflect the company's potential, but there is plenty more to consider.
